open_points.subject: failure entry cardinality
open_points.text: one entry for each failing input or record, each naming the field or the identity it concerns; within one kind, entries are ordered first by the record or input they concern — inputs in the order the operation's Inputs list them, then records list by list in that same order, each list in its own order (A06) — and then, within one record or input, by its fields in the order its Inputs or model lists them.
open_points.question: When one input or record has failures in two fields of the same error kind, is the answer one entry for the record, one entry per failing field, or one entry containing several fields?
options: One entry per failing input or record, naming only its identity
One entry per failing field, so one record may produce several entries
One entry per failing input or record containing all of its failing fields
open_points.default_guess: Return one entry per failing field, because otherwise the answer cannot name every failure or apply the stated field ordering.

witness.initial: One submitted record has two fields that fail the same stage and error kind.
events: The record module detects both failing fields.
The operation assembles the first failing stage's error answer.
outcomes: The answer contains one entry for the record.
The answer contains two entries, ordered by the fields.
witness.observer: The caller comparing the error array's length and contents

open_points.subject: input-versus-model field ordering
open_points.text: by its fields in the order its Inputs or model lists them.
open_points.question: For a value represented both by an operation input structure and by a model, which declaration supplies the field order when their orders differ, and how are embedded model fields flattened?
options: Use the operation's Inputs order for all submitted values
Use the model's order whenever a model describes the value
Use Inputs for top-level fields and recursively use each embedded model's order
open_points.default_guess: Use Inputs for top-level input fields and recursively use the applicable model order inside an embedded record.

witness.initial: An operation's Inputs list field A before embedded record B, while the model declaration or its recursive flattening places a failing field of B before A.
events: The caller supplies invalid values for A and for a field inside B.
Both failures have the same error kind.
The operation orders the error entries.
outcomes: The failure for A is returned first by following Inputs order.
The failure inside B is returned first by following model order.
witness.observer: The caller observing the order of error entries

open_points.subject: ordering nested record lists
open_points.text: then records list by list in that same order, each list in its own order (A06)
open_points.question: When records are in nested lists, such as each imported project's rooms and pointers, is ordering parent-major or list-kind-major, and what exact sequence of lists does “that same order” denote?
options: For each project in order, emit its rooms in order and then its pointers in order
Emit all projects, then all rooms grouped by project, then all pointers grouped by project
Treat every nested list as a separate list in the order it is first encountered by the operation
open_points.default_guess: Use parent-major traversal: each project in order, then that project's rooms and pointers in their A06 orders.

witness.initial: Two picked import projects each contain a malformed room and a malformed pointer, all reported under one error kind.
events: The owner asks for the import mapping.
The import checks both projects and their nested records.
The mapping orders the four malformed-record entries.
outcomes: Project 1's room and pointer precede Project 2's room and pointer.
Both rooms precede both pointers, with projects ordered inside each group.
witness.observer: The owner interface rendering the mapping and any test comparing its ordered errors

open_points.subject: pass resumption deadline
open_points.text: the next call is the first deadline at or after the reading when the pass can run again; a deadline equal to that reading is made.
open_points.question: What event fixes “the reading when the pass can run again”: the instant the host resumes or the previous call finishes, the scheduler's first actual execution afterward, or a scheduled deadline; and may an already-due deadline run late if the reading occurs just after it?
options: Take a monotonic reading immediately when the blocking condition ends and schedule the first deadline at or after it
Use the first reading the scheduler actually obtains after it can execute, skipping every earlier deadline
Preserve a scheduled deadline and make its call late when execution is delayed past it
open_points.default_guess: Read immediately when the host resumes or the previous call finishes, schedule the first deadline at or after that reading, and skip it if execution cannot begin before a later reading has passed it.

witness.initial: Serving began at monotonic reading 0 with a 60-second interval; the host becomes runnable just before reading 60, but the pass code first executes and reads the clock just after 60.
events: The host is suspended across most of the interval.
The host becomes runnable immediately before the deadline.
Scheduling delay prevents the pass from reading the clock until immediately after the deadline.
outcomes: The 60-second call is made because the pass could run again before its deadline.
The 60-second call is skipped because the actual reading is after it, and the next call is due at 120.
witness.observer: The owner observing when an expired session is removed, or the host observing when the backup look occurs
